findings.title: Do not interpret a legacy array-valued feature named profile as an opt-in marker
findings.source_observation: read() finds any features.profile and rejects unless profile.as_str()==Some(constrained-r1). CandidateMetadata::from_bytes calls it before legacy Manifest::parse_str. Legacy FeaturesTable permits any ordinary feature key including profile with an array of effects.
findings.consequence: Previously valid absent/legacy local package metadata fails as unknown authored profile. Direct ordinary parser can still parse it, so the new metadata path violates explicit legacy preservation.
findings.minimal_correction: Discriminate the explicit marker shape without reserving an existing array-valued legacy feature name. Return no opt-in for a valid legacy array-valued profile feature; retain strict unknown-string-profile and malformed constrained profile refusal. Add one arm to existing core compatibility case; no new matrix.

findings.title: Do not demand consumer input from every unselected catalog candidate
findings.related_lines: same file278–288 early missing-definitions check; package-source/source.rs bind_request new unconditional call
findings.source_observation: admit_source_definitions iterates self.inspect().candidates and requires current configuration plus matching caller instance for every metadata.checked_features row. solve_configuration_routes also rejects any checked-profile inventory row absent from definitions before SAT selection. Base C1 capture traverses all versions, recommends, requires_any alternatives and target dependencies (catalog.rs45–69), so inventory contains unselected alternatives.
findings.consequence: A valid solution using a different technical alternative/discarded version is refused merely because an unused constrained Redbook candidate is in the captured inventory and has no incoming consumer edge. This moves a selection need to discovery/pre-solve and violates preserved C2 unreachable-candidate behavior.
findings.concrete_source_scenario: A normal captured root offers requires_any=[unconstrained viable alternative, Redbook] and another root/constraint excludes Redbook, or an unused constrained version/dependency exists only in a discarded candidate. No Redbook consumer instance is needed by the selected solution, yet bind_request errors missing original consumer instance before the solver can choose the other valid path.
findings.minimal_correction: Retain/capture and validate immutable package definitions independently of current consumer demand; bind only actual caller consumer inputs and make missing input/definitions conditional on candidate participation through the incumbent candidate-conditioned need/refusal mechanism. Never fabricate domains/default consent, treat a selected unbound profile as legacy required-all, or weaken selected definition/receipt equality. One bounded discarded-alternative arm in the existing resolver story suffices; no generic caller/CLI parity requirement.
